title: Capitolo 10 · Health — the body, the doctor and the pharmacy
shortDescription: The parts of the body and saying what hurts (ho mal di…, mi fa / mi fanno male, ho la febbre), at the doctor's and at the pharmacy (la ricetta, lo sciroppo, le compresse, la pomata), the direct object pronouns lo, la, li, le, and the imperative for advice and instructions — informal (prendi!) and formal (prenda!).
description:
Part of the official SS Europa Italian course used in our classes, for learners from India, Pakistan and Bangladesh who are going to Italy to work, study or live. Chapters 1–7 take you from zero to level A1 and Chapters 8–12 to level A2 — study them in order.

Every 60-minute class of the chapter is split into three short lessons you can study on your phone, with pictures, audio, grammar tables and exercises. Every word comes with its English and Punjabi meaning, the slides of each class are attached as PDF, and the chapter ends with a test (pass mark 60%).
objectives:
I can name the main parts of the body
I can say what hurts: ho mal di testa, mi fa male la schiena, mi fanno male le gambe
I can explain my symptoms to the doctor and ask for a prescription
I can buy medicine at the pharmacy and understand how to take it
I can avoid repeating nouns with lo, la, li, le: Prendi lo sciroppo? Sì, lo prendo
I can give advice to a friend (riposa, non uscire!) and understand formal instructions (prenda, firmi qui)

blocks.title: Ricorda
blocks.body:
- **lo** = il / lo (masc. sing.) · **la** = la (fem. sing.)
- **li** = i / gli (masc. pl.) · **le** = le (fem. pl.)
- Always **before** the verb: *lo prendo, non lo prendo* · joined to an infinitive: *devo prenderlo*

blocks.title: Test Capitolo 10
blocks.body:
This test checks everything in Chapter 10 (Lessons 1–4).

- **1. Listening** — sentences and a dialogue at the doctor's
- **2. Vocabulary** — body, symptoms, doctor and pharmacy
- **3. Grammar** — mi fa / mi fanno male, lo / la / li / le, the imperative (tu and Lei)
- **4. Writing** — symptoms and health advice

You need **60%** to pass. You can repeat the test as many times as you like.
